--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.node_disjoint_paths()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Find the largest set of paths between two nodes that share no intermediate node. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.node_disjoint_paths()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Find the largest set of paths between two nodes that share no intermediate node. title: >- [Graph.node_disjoint_paths()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Find the largest set of paths between two nodes that share no intermediate node. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the largest set of paths between two nodes that share no intermediate node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L71790-L71911){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.node_disjoint_paths( source, target, max_paths=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Node-disjoint paths](../assets/graphs/node-disjoint-paths.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same graph: two triangles sharing node C, plus a detour from A to E through F. Only two paths from A to E avoid each other's inner nodes, A, C, E in the accent color and A, F, E in teal; the third edge-disjoint route, A, B, C, D, E, would reuse C, so B and D stay faint." width="100%"} Node-disjoint (or internally disjoint) paths share only their two endpoints: no node in between is used twice. This is a stronger requirement than edge-disjointness, since a single failed node can no longer break more than one route. By Menger's theorem, the largest number of such paths equals the number of nodes that must be removed to separate the endpoints (`node_connectivity_between()`). The paths come from a maximum flow in which every node other than the endpoints can carry one unit, decomposed into individual routes. Directed graphs are followed in edge direction. If the endpoints are adjacent, the direct edge counts as one path. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The starting node, as an integer ID or a string label. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The destination node, as an integer ID or a string label. [max_paths]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stop after finding this many paths. If `None` (default), find as many as possible. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The paths as lists of node IDs from `source=` to `target=`, shortest first. Empty if the target is unreachable. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist, `source=` equals `target=`, or `max_paths=` is below 1. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~edge_disjoint_paths`) : Paths that may share nodes but not edges. [](`~node_connectivity_between`) : The number of paths, by Menger's theorem. [](`~minimum_node_cut`) : The nodes that limit the number of paths. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In the same bowtie, the shared node C means A and E have only one node-disjoint route, even though they have two edge-disjoint ones: ::: {#31d9f172 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec bowtie = ec.Graph.from_edges( [ ("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "C"), ] ) ( len(bowtie.node_disjoint_paths("A", "E")), len(bowtie.edge_disjoint_paths("A", "E")), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (1, 2) ``` ::: ::: A cube has three node-disjoint routes between opposite corners, one through each neighbor of the start: ::: {#86682ef3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} cube = ec.Graph.from_edges( [ (str(a), str(b)) for a in range(8) for b in range(a + 1, 8) if bin(a ^ b).count("1") == 1 ] ) label = cube.get_label_from_id [[label(n) for n in path] for path in cube.node_disjoint_paths("0", "7")] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [['0', '1', '3', '7'], ['0', '2', '6', '7'], ['0', '4', '5', '7']] ``` ::: ::: ### Separate chains of friends Zachary's karate club split in two after a dispute between its instructor (member 0) and its administrator (member 33). The two leaders are joined by ten chains of friendships that share no friendship, but only six that share no member, one through each of the six members of `minimum_node_cut()`: ::: {#4aafcb6a .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club() chains = karate.node_disjoint_paths("0", "33") label = karate.get_label_from_id len(karate.edge_disjoint_paths("0", "33")), [ [label(n) for n in chain] for chain in chains ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (10, [['0', '8', '33'], ['0', '13', '33'], ['0', '19', '33'], ['0', '31', '33'], ['0', '1', '30', '33'], ['0', '2', '9', '33']]) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#3d9f93c6 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} links = { (u, v): i + 1 for i, chain in enumerate(chains) for u, v in zip(chain, chain[1:]) } karate.set_edge_attrs("chain", list(links.values()), edges=list(links)) karate.set_edge_attrs("on_chain", {e: 0 for e in karate.get_edge_ids()}) karate.set_edge_attrs("on_chain", 1, edges=list(links)) karate.layout_kamada_kawai().plot( layout="pos", edge_color_by="chain", edge_width_by="on_chain", edge_opacity=0.9, label_by="label", ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
